description:
How to survive a nuclear blast hour by hour in the suburbs comes down to a few decisions made in the first minutes. The biggest mistake may be doing what feels most natural. Getting in your car and trying to escape. In many scenarios, staying underground and waiting can dramatically improve your chances of survival.

This video follows a suburban family through the first 48 hours after a nuclear detonation, explaining what happens from the initial warning and flash to the blast wave, radioactive fallout, and the dangerous hours that follow. We explore why basements provide crucial radiation shielding, how Protection Factor works, and why cars offer almost no protection from fallout.
You’ll also learn about the 7/10 Rule, why radiation levels fall rapidly with time, when fallout is most dangerous, and how simple decontamination steps such as removing outer clothing and washing with soap and water can significantly reduce exposure.

description:
Why do athletes smoke weed? For some, cannabis isn’t about getting high before competition. It’s about pain relief, recovery, anxiety, sleep, and avoiding stronger prescription drugs. Yet athletes can still face suspensions and lost opportunities for using a substance that research suggests may offer little direct performance advantage.

This video examines the controversy through cases like Sha’Carri Richardson and Olympic snowboarder Ross Rebagliati, while exploring why organizations such as WADA continue to restrict cannabis. We look at the history of drug use in sport, the origins of marijuana prohibition, and how decades of political and cultural stigma shaped modern anti-doping rules.
We also explore what cannabis may actually do for athletes. Research suggests it can make pain feel more manageable, improve mood during exercise, and reduce anxiety for some users. At the same time, it can negatively affect coordination, reaction time, and lung health when smoked.
